# GitSettle

> GitHub contribution escrow on NEAR: maintainers fund issues, contributors submit pull requests, a trusted verifier authorizes settlement, and the contract records successful rewards and reputation. Built by CodeMaster Labs for NEAR HACKATHON, November 2026.

## Project and status

- Repository: https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle
- Live testnet app: https://gitsettle.89.167.109.196.sslip.io
- Network: NEAR testnet only. Rewards: native NEAR. Storage charge: 0.05 NEAR, permanent and nonrefundable.
- Contract: gitsettle-ac1b0f23f4.testnet. Verifier: verifier.gitsettle-ac1b0f23f4.testnet.
- Verification snapshot: November 14, 2026; deployed application source 5c8dc527b3d6d29f6773ff6ac402c5886083f512. Later documentation commits do not change the recorded runtime.
- CI: 41 Rust tests, 182 Node tests and 146 browser tests passed; one intentional mobile global-search skip (147 browser scenarios discovered).
- Hosted advisory AI is disabled. AI/provider fixtures do not establish real paid model calls or third-party wallet approvals.
- No GitSettle MCP server, AgentGuard vault custody, TEE execution, on-chain risk-oracle integration or NEAR Intents integration is claimed.

## Implementation and usage

- [Architecture](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md): contract authority, web/verifier data flow, SQLite responsibilities and extension points.
- [NEAR contract](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle/tree/main/contracts/gitsettle) and [contract API](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle/blob/main/docs/CONTRACT_API.md): escrow, state transitions, release/refund access control, transfer recovery and top-100 reputation.
- [Verifier](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle/tree/main/services/verifier): merge after funding, repository/issue/claimant binding, exact locale paths, changed-file pagination, duplicate PR and local risk checks.
- [Web app](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle/tree/main/apps/web): posting, queue, wallet actions, contributor profiles, maintainer dashboard and private support.
- [CLI reference](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle/blob/main/docs/CLI.md): finalized reads, transaction previews and protected local signing. Workspace executable; no standalone npm publication is claimed.
- [Wallet capabilities](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle/blob/main/docs/WALLETS.md): MyNearWallet, Meteor, Intear and Nightly. Intear's adapter supports escrow but cannot authenticate private support; provider approval verification limits are documented.
- [Support](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle/blob/main/docs/COMMUNITY.md) and [triage](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle/blob/main/docs/TRIAGE.md): wallet sessions, private ACLs, duplicate/spam checks, advisory AI configuration and quotas.
- [Self-hosting](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle/blob/main/docs/SELF_HOST.md): own contract/verifier, Docker/VPS, persistent data and isolated credentials.
- [UI review](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle/blob/main/docs/UI_REVIEW.md): real live screenshots separately from labeled demo/fixture captures.
- [Presentation and reproduction](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle/blob/main/DEMO.md): existing payout walkthrough and a separate fresh testnet payout workflow.

## Quick reproduction

Local browsing: git clone https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle.git; cd gitsettle; docker compose up --build --detach --wait. Open http://localhost:3000. A fresh installation without .env uses labeled example data and disables signing; demo IDs are 0-7, while recorded live bounty 8 belongs to the public testnet deployment.

Read-only CLI, with Node 22.22.2+ from the checkout: npm ci; npm run cli -- show 8 --json; npm run cli -- leaderboard --json. No private key is needed. The CLI defaults to the documented testnet contract and finalized RPC. Mutations require protected local credentials and explicit confirmation.

## Sister project and reused baseline

- [AgentGuard](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/agentguard): a separate NEAR hackathon project by CodeMaster Labs for owner-controlled AI-agent spending vaults, on-chain limits, approval queues and optional signed TEE risk-oracle verdicts.
- [AgentGuard app](https://agentguard-beryl.vercel.app), [1:56 demo](https://agentguard-beryl.vercel.app/agentguard-demo.mp4), and [its AI index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CodeMasterLabs/agentguard/main/llms.txt): its capabilities and evidence belong to that project.
- [GitSettle integration disclosure](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle/blob/main/docs/AGENTGUARD.md): exact vendored MIT recipient/text heuristic files, hashes and upstream commit 4ec34e69bc7c6cfd17a3e027bf9727a67eab97f6. GitSettle adds its own exact per-payout cap and conservative review holds in the trusted worker.
- [Reciprocal disclosure](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/agentguard#related-project-disclosure): shared developer and distinct product scope. Reused heuristics are not newly authored GitSettle work.

## Trust boundaries and limits

- The verifier is trusted: NEAR cannot read GitHub. The poster may also authorize release directly. A compromised verifier/poster can approve undeserved payment to the recorded claimant, but release cannot choose a different payee.
- The deployment retains a full-access upgrade key. It is an unaudited, operator-controlled testnet MVP.
- PR markers are not cryptographic GitHub identity proofs. Verification checks evidence structure, not code quality, translation accuracy or GitHub issue closure. Reputation counts successful authorized payouts and is not Sybil resistant.
- Submitted work remains protected after its deadline, potentially indefinitely. There is no submission-expiry court, binding dispute adjudication or claim lease/cancellation. Eligible Open/Claimed/Rejected rewards may be refunded at/after the deadline.
- AgentGuard heuristics run locally and can be bypassed by the signer or poster; they can have false positives/negatives. The default automatic cap is 5 NEAR per payout, not a daily budget.
- Support is operator-readable, not end-to-end encrypted. Appeals do not pause deadlines, block eligible refunds or reverse payments. Optional AI is advisory and can be wrong.
- GitHub/RPC availability, rate limits and GitHub's 3,000-file cap constrain automatic checks. Initial operation assumes one verifier process and SQLite on one host.
- [Security review](https://github.com/CodeMasterLabs/gitsettle/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_REVIEW.md) documents dependency findings and remaining limits.
- Application license is MIT. Separately reused wallet executors retain their upstream licenses, including AGPL/MIT disclosures for Intear; see third_party/intear and WALLETS.md.

## Hackathon fit

GitSettle's implemented track scope: social (issue rewards, translations, reputation/support), open (original NEAR escrow and self-hosted web/CLI stack), agents (deterministic verification/payout worker). GitSettle and AgentGuard are distinct projects with a disclosed shared baseline. GitSettle was built from an empty workspace on November 14, 2026 with AI coding assistance. Submission and the demo post belong to the project owner.
